subject: Post-call: regional support privileges and data residency follow-up
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@northbridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: regional support privileges and data residency follow-up

Alex — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap + asks so we can align with Legal/Sec and share a short mutual action plan.

Call highlights (your notes + mine):
- You're evaluating Redwood for a user-facing assistant that will process limited PII (name, email, short support messages).
- Data residency requirement: production inference must run in us-west region, logs retained for 30 days, with option for 365d archival on request.
- Support model: you want scoped support access (just request IDs and limited logs), strict RBAC, and a documented break-glass process for high-severity incidents.

Immediate asks from your side:
1) Example support entitlements (who sees what) — can we provide a matrix?
2) Confirmation of log retention/rotation and what gets excluded from logs (full user content vs metadata).
3) Break-glass workflow and audit logging for any elevation.

Next steps from Redwood (what I'll coordinate):
- Ben: can you draft a scoped support matrix + what we can provide as evidence (audit logs, session sampling policy)?
- Marissa: can you confirm whether the 30d default retention with opt-in archival is acceptable from a compliance viewpoint and note any contract language we should propose?

Attaching our privacy FAQ and a lightweight support matrix template for reference. I'll follow up with a short one-pager we can share with your legal/security team.

Thanks — Irene

--
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@northbridge.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Northbridge Security <security@northbridge.ai>, procurement@northbridge.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: regional support privileges and data residency follow-up

Thanks, Irene — that recap is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- Residency: us-west is fine for inference, but audit logs must be stored in an EU location for our EU customers (we can discuss a hybrid retention policy). Is that supported or do logs always co-reside with compute?
- Scoped support: we need support agents to be able to view anonymized request metadata and to request a full transcript only with documented approval (ticket + exec signoff).
- Break-glass: please include the timestamps required in the audit trail (who elevated, duration, reason).

Also tagging security — can you confirm the minimum packet of evidence you need for a SOC-type review (policy docs, sample logs, SOC2 questions answered)? Procurement will want an estimate of any additional implementation/ops fees if we request regional log segregation.

— Alex
Alex Garcia
Senior Product Manager, Integrations
Northbridge AI
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@northbridge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: regional support privileges and data residency follow-up

Alex — quick answers from Support/Oncall perspective:

1) Support access model (summary):
- Tiered roles: Support Agent (view metadata + sanitized context), Support Engineer (view full request bodies when approved), Oncall Lead (can request break-glass but requires written justification).
- Access is RBAC-driven via SSO groups; we can map to your AD groups during onboarding.

2) Logs and residency:
- Runtime inference telemetry (latency, error rates) stays in compute region. Request/response logs can be routed to a separate storage bucket; we can create a pipeline to mirror logs to an EU bucket for EU-customer requests. That is additional ops (export pipeline + ACL controls).

3) Break-glass flow (initial proposal):
- Trigger ticket created (incidents.redwood.io/ID) + executive approval email recorded.
- Elevation window automatically audited with user, time, and IP. All break-glass events write immutably to the audit index.

I'll attach a draft support-access-matrix for you to review and mark up. Ben

--
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability
ben@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@northbridge.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 08:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: regional support privileges and data residency follow-up

Alex — Kopied the highlights for Legal/Security intake. A few compliance notes:

- PII handling: please confirm the PII classes we should treat as sensitive. Our standard is to treat name/email as low-sensitivity unless paired with identifiers (SSN, payment data). If you consider name/email high-sensitivity for your use-case, we need to flag this in contract clauses and potentially limit retention.
- Retention: default 30d for request logs is fine; for EU mirroring we will need a data processing addendum outlining where logs are stored and who has access.
- Evidence pack: we can provide the following for an initial review: SOC2 summary, redacted sample logs (anonymized), support-access matrix, and incident audit export. If you require full raw logs for review, that will need a data sharing agreement.

If procurement needs language, suggest: 1) audit logs mirror to EU only for EU-account requests, 2) Redwood will produce break-glass audit exports within 5 business days. Happy to draft CLA-friendly text.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Security & Compliance (advisor to Sales)
marissa@redwood.com
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@northbridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, procurement@northbridge.ai

Subject: Re: Post-call: regional support privileges and data residency follow-up

Alex — appreciate the quick responses and the security tag-in. Short plan and asks so we can put this into a MAT and get procurement feedback: 

1) Ben will upload the support-access-matrix (attached) with three sample scenarios (agent view, engineer view, break-glass).
2) Marissa will draft suggested contract language for data mirror + break-glass audit export SLA.
3) Irene (me) will share the one-pager for Legal + open a HubSpot task under deal NB-2027-032 referencing the required evidence pack.

Please review the attached matrix and flag any rows you absolutely need changed (e.g., if agents must never see anonymized content at all). Also let us know whether the EU log mirror is required at POC stage (ops cost estimate depends on this).

Attachments: redwood_privacy_faq.pdf, support-access-matrix.xlsx

Looking forward to next steps — we can schedule a technical touchpoint with Ben and your security team early next week.

Thanks — Irene
